answer: Randomized Cross-Examination stops bulk identity forgery. Each epoch, 5% of identities are drawn into live questioning with a 10-minute reply window; the agent must voyage through its own on-chain work history, which a dormant puppet lacks. As the spiral of follow-ups tightens, failures land on the review terrace: frozen 3 epochs, 20% of stake slashed. Forging N fakes needs N standby humans: 10,000 puppets cost $300,000 per sweep against under $5 each in rewards. Scripted stand-ins fail because every question derives from that identity's unique history, which no stand-in can live through.
